title: Custom providers and the model list — first look

steps.path: Settings → Assistant settings → Cloud providers → Add provider
steps.headline: Add provider starts with one search box for the service, instead of a type list and a blank name.
steps.changed: The Type dropdown (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, "Custom endpoint (OpenAI-compatible)") becomes a Service box you type into. The Name and key boxes appear once a service is picked.
steps.notice: You type a service you have heard of. Nothing asks you to invent a name or know what an endpoint is before you start.
steps.risk: Someone who already knows their address takes one extra step: pick "Other address…" first.

steps.headline: Typing narrows about 190 services to the ones that match, with "Other address…" always at the bottom.
steps.changed: The list comes from the public catalog the app already downloads for prices; only services that publish their address are offered.
steps.measured: 206 services listed with an address on models.dev (2026-10-20)
steps.notice: Inception, DeepSeek, Groq-style services are one word away. A service missing from the list still works through Other address.
steps.risk: The practice app has 15 services; the real list (~190) is checked after the build.

steps.headline: Picking a service fills the name, says where it connects and how many models it has, and asks for the key.
steps.changed: The name is filled from the service and stays editable. A grey line under the box shows the address and model count. The key is required here, not "optional".
steps.notice: One paste and Add provider. You can see what you are connecting to before you press anything.
steps.risk: The model count is the public catalog's; your account may see a few more or fewer.

steps.headline: "Other address…" keeps the old way in, for a home server or a service not on the list.
steps.changed: An Address box appears, the key is marked optional (home servers often have none), and the hint names Ollama as an example.
steps.notice: Nothing you could connect before is lost. A local address still moves to Local models, now with a line saying so.

steps.path: Add provider → paste a key → Add provider
steps.headline: Adding checks the connection right away; a working provider says how many models it brings.
steps.changed: Add provider now saves and then checks. The row's grey line reads "Connected · 4 models". Edit replaces Add key / Replace key and opens the same form.
steps.notice: You know it works before you go to a chat. A wrong address no longer means Remove and add again.
steps.risk: The button reads "Checking…" for a second or two.

steps.path: Add provider → paste a wrong key → Add provider
steps.headline: A key that doesn't work is still saved, and the problem sits on the row with Edit and Try again.
steps.changed: The failed check becomes one red notice inside the row, its fixes beside it; the row reads "Not connected" until it passes.
steps.notice: A typo shows up here, next to its fix — not later as a confusing error in a chat.
steps.risk: A bad key stays listed until you fix or remove it.

steps.path: Chat → model menu → search for a model that isn't listed
steps.headline: A search that finds nothing offers "Check for new models" instead of a dead end.
steps.changed: Under "No models match." a full-width button asks every connected service for its latest list, skipping the once-a-day wait.
steps.notice: A model released this morning — Mercury 3 yesterday — is one press away instead of a day away.
steps.risk: Only shown where the picker has a search (assistant sessions), so Claude Code's own menu is unchanged.

steps.path: Model menu → search "mercury" → Check for new models
steps.headline: After the check, the same search runs again against the new list.
steps.changed: The button shows "Checking for new models…" while it runs; the search stays as you typed it, and new models appear in place.
steps.notice: You never retype the search. If nothing new turned up, the line says the list is up to date.

steps.path: Model menu → Check for new models, while a service is down
steps.headline: If a service can't be reached, the notice names it, says your list is unchanged, and offers Try again.
steps.changed: A red notice replaces the button, naming the list that failed. Lists that did answer still update.
steps.notice: A failed check never empties your model list, and it says which service to blame.
